Dalia: heads-up — on a small T4 fleet after the 537 driver bump I'm seeing kernel handoffs that weren't there before. short seqlen (<64) requests are getting routed to the generic matmul path instead of our fastpath_v2. p95 latency +6% on the canary cluster.
Kai: ugh. do we have a repro script / probe output?
Dalia: yes, ran a quick probe and a microbench. probe dump:
```
probe --gpu=0 --capdump
SM=75
tensor_cores=present
bf16: supported
fp8: unsupported
kernel_hint: seqlen<=64 -> fastpath_v2
selected_kernel: matmul_generic
```
Ravi: interesting — driver expose changed something in the feature flags, maybe our hw fingerprint is now returning an extra cap that flips heuristic ordering.
Lena: could also be hysteresis/oscillation: fastpath picks count on seqlen distribution + recent throughput. if the prefix cache warms differently after the driver, our rolling counters might fall below the threshold and trigger the fallback.
ben-eng: i saw similar on a mixed farm last month, caused by batching heuristics changing when requests with cached KV prefixes show near-zero compute cost but still bump batch size. batching -> kernel route bad combo.
Dalia: microbench numbers (canary): baseline fastpath_v2 8ms p95 for seqlen32. matmul_generic 8.5ms p95, but under bursty mixed loads matmul_generic becomes 9.5-10ms. CPU-side overhead minimal.
perf-bot: benchmark results uploaded: https://perf.internal/runs/1749123456
Kai: hypothesis: driver/cc change changed fp8/bf16 reporting path which alters our kernel selection table lookup order. fallback rule order is fragile.
Ravi: two action paths: 1) hardpin selection by SM major/minor and explicit tensorcore/bf16 flags before heuristics, 2) smooth the route decision with a hysteresis window (time+count) to prevent flips for transient distribution shifts.
Lena: i prefer (2) first — quick mitigation. Add a 30s smoothing window + require 3 consecutive bucket flips before switching kernel. Also differentiate cold vs warm KV cache: if prefix cache hit ratio > 0.7, prefer fastpath.
Dalia: agreed. quick patch idea (pseudocode):
```
route = current_route
if candidate != current_route:
  flips[candidate] += 1
  if flips[candidate] >= 3 and time_since(last_switch) > 30s:
    current_route = candidate
else:
  flips = {}
```
ben-eng: +1, but let's also log route-reason + hw-sig on each decision for 24h to debug root cause.
Kai: i'll run a focused microbench that toggles KV warm/cold with seqlen 8/32/128 and driver 537 vs 540 images. I'll post raw flamegraphs.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: eng-runtime/handoff-hysteresis/patch-1 -> canary cluster at 02:15 UTC
Ravi: for long-term, we should move kernel selection to a deterministic table keyed by (SM, driver-hash, tensorcore, bf16, fp8, seqlen-range) with a fallback precedence order. That avoids relying on noisy runtime counters.
Dalia: agreed. add item to runtime roadmap. For now Kai will own the canary run, Lena will prep the quick hysteresis patch, ben-eng will add logging. if canary looks good we'll roll to prod.
Kai: starting runs now. posting results in ~25m :eyes:
Lena: i'll open the PR and tag @ops for the canary rollout checklist.
Dalia: thanks all — if we see any p99 blips ping @oncall immediately.
